trial_court: Sessions Judge, Goalpara in Criminal Appeal No.3/2007
case_name: Sri Bhupen Nath v. The State of Assam & Smti. Dipti Rani Devi

parties.respondent_defendant: The State of Assam & Smti. Dipti Rani Devi

outcome_detected: The judgment of the lower Court is upheld
facts_of_case: Petitioner was convicted under Section 494 of IPC and sentenced for 1 year Rigorous Imprisonment with fine of Rs. 3,000/- in default to undergo 6(six) months of Simple Imprisonment.

legal_principles.principle: A Hindu marriage must be solemnized in accordance with the applicable customs or usage.
legal_principles.held: Therefore, requisite ceremonies for the solemnisation of the Hindu marriage must be in accordance with the applicable customs or usage and where saptapadi has been adopted, the marriage becomes complete and binding when the seventh step is taken.

legal_principles.principle: The requisite ceremonies for a Hindu marriage must be performed and there must be proof of performance when an issue or controversy arises.
legal_principles.held: Therefore, the requisite ceremonies have to be performed and there must be proof of performance of the said ceremony when an issue/controversy arise.

legal_principles.principle: A Hindu marriage is not valid if the requisite ceremonies are not performed.
legal_principles.held: Where a Hindu marriage is not performed in accordance with the applicable rites or ceremonies such as saptapadi when included, the marriage will not be construed as a Hindu marriage.

outcome.final_order: The judgment of the lower Court is upheld.
